messages.subject: ggvis+shiny issue
parts:
Trying to learn the tricks of getting the Shiny+ggvis combo to do what I want. I think I have read through every single post on this and I'm still stumped on why I can't get the following example to work. So now I must appeal to the gurus :) 

Here is the example: 

library(shiny)
library(ggvis)

shinyUI(fluidPage(

  # Application title
  titlePanel("Shiny/ggvis Test"),

  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      
      selectInput("x.var", "X:",choices=names(mtcars),selected='mph'),
      selectInput("y.var", "Y:",choices=names(mtcars),selected='hp')
      
    ),
    mainPanel(
      ggvisOutput("theplot")
    )
  )
))

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  
  selectedData <- reactive({
    mtcars[, c(input$x.var, input$y.var)]
  })
  
  varNames <- reactive({
    names(selectedData())
  })
  
  selectedData() %>% 
    ggvis(x = as.name(varNames()[1]), y = as.name(varNames()[2])) %>%    
    layer_points() %>%
    add_tooltip(all_values,"hover") %>%
    bind_shiny("theplot")
  
  all_values <- function(x){
    if(is.null(x)) return(NULL)
    paste0(names(x), ": ", format(x), collapse = "<br />")
  }
  
})



This gives me the error: 

Error in .getReactiveEnvironment()$currentContext() : 
  Operation not allowed without an active reactive context. (You tried to do something that can only be done from inside a reactive expression or observer.)

So somehow I must be accessing something that should be in a reactive, right? But I don't know what. 

Session Info: ggvis 0.3.0.1, shiny 0.10.0, R 3.1.0

- Karsten

messages.author: 1161df5ae7a276da
messages.subject: Re: ggvis+shiny issue
parts:
Hi Karsten,

I got this to almost work - if you don't care about axes labels, it works completely.

I've been twiddling with this myself - a few points:

I have discovered that ggvis takes "naked" reactives. I'm sure Winston and Hadley will have a better way to describe it, but ggvis, does not take the data that the reactive provides, instead takes the name of the reactive that provides it. Hence, the parentheses are removed from selectedData.

I made reactives that provide the names of the variables as "names"  (you were on the right track). Apparently, I have to tell ggvis to construct a scale (I don't know why, but it seems to work).

Here's the remaining issue: Vega does not let ggvis update the name of an axis label. (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/ggvis/ZJXdIFAmb68) Winston can let me know if I have misinterpreted this.

Server code below.

Hope this helps.

Ian

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  
  selectedData <- reactive({
    mtcars[, c(input$x.var, input$y.var)]
  })

rct_name_x <- reactive({
    as.name(input$x.var) 
  })

  rct_name_y <- reactive({
    as.name(input$y.var) 
  })
  
  selectedData %>% 
    ggvis(
      prop("x", rct_name_x, scale = TRUE), 
      prop("y", rct_name_y, scale = TRUE)

) %>%    
    layer_points() %>%
    add_tooltip(all_values, "hover") %>%
    bind_shiny("theplot")
  
  all_values <- function(x){
    if(is.null(x)) return(NULL)
    paste0(names(x), ": ", format(x), collapse = "<br />")
  }
  
})

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: ggvis+shiny issue
parts:
That's right - ggvis can take "bare" reactives as data sources; when the data changes, the updated data is processed and sent to the browser for rendering. 

You can also put the whole ggvis call in a reactive() block, but this behaves a bit differently: instead of simply updating the data, the entire plot spec (a JSON description of the plot) is sent to the browser and the plot is rebuilt from scratch. This will take a bit more time than simply updating the data, and it will also result in a blanking out of the plotting area while it's re-rendered.

At the moment the data in a plot can be changed without sending a new spec, but other parts can't. For example, the plot title and axis titles can't be changed simply by updating the data.

-Winston

Hi Karsten,

I got this to almost work - if you don't care about axes labels, it works completely.

I've been twiddling with this myself - a few points:

I have discovered that ggvis takes "naked" reactives. I'm sure Winston and Hadley will have a better way to describe it, but ggvis, does not take the data that the reactive provides, instead takes the name of the reactive that provides it. Hence, the parentheses are removed from selectedData.

I made reactives that provide the names of the variables as "names"  (you were on the right track). Apparently, I have to tell ggvis to construct a scale (I don't know why, but it seems to work).

Here's the remaining issue: Vega does not let ggvis update the name of an axis label. (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/ggvis/ZJXdIFAmb68) Winston can let me know if I have misinterpreted this.

Server code below.

Hope this helps.

Ian



shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {
  
  selectedData <- reactive({
    mtcars[, c(input$x.var, input$y.var)]
  })
  
  rct_name_x <- reactive({
    as.name(input$x.var) 
  })

  rct_name_y <- reactive({
    as.name(input$y.var) 
  })
  
  selectedData %>% 
    ggvis(
      prop("x", rct_name_x, scale = TRUE), 
      prop("y", rct_name_y, scale = TRUE)
    ) %>%    
    layer_points() %>%
    add_tooltip(all_values, "hover") %>%
    bind_shiny("theplot")
  
  all_values <- function(x){
    if(is.null(x)) return(NULL)
    paste0(names(x), ": ", format(x), collapse = "<br />")
  }
  
})
